title: Where it grows
subtitle: Islands and coasts
objectives: Explain its role in Provence rosé

steps.title: Sardinia and Corsica
steps.body: Sardinia is Vermentino's stronghold. Vermentino di Gallura, in the granite north-east, is the island's only DOCG, since 1996, giving fuller, more structured, saline wines. Vermentino di Sardegna DOC covers the whole island. In Corsica, Vermentino, also called Vermentinu, makes Patrimonio and Ajaccio whites.

steps.title: Tuscany, Liguria and Provence
steps.body: Tuscany's coast, Bolgheri and the Maremma, makes fresh Vermentino. Liguria's Cinque Terre and Riviera Ligure di Ponente use it and Pigato. In Provence, Rolle is the main white grape and is often blended into rosé to add freshness and aroma. Australia is planting it as a heat-tolerant grape.

steps.explanation: Vermentino di Gallura, from the granite north-east, became DOCG in 1996.

steps.body: In Provence rosé, a share of Rolle adds freshness and a floral, citrus lift. Check the back label: many pale rosés include it.

steps.explanation: The Mosel is too cold; it's Riesling country.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Sardinia's Vermentino di Gallura is its DOCG
Corsica, coastal Tuscany and Liguria grow it
In Provence it's Rolle, often in rosé
